strategy.summary: Reproduce pandas PR #66175 (GH#49631): Sparse[datetime64] with NaT fill cast to Sparse[int64] via string or explicit SparseDtype should map NaT to iNaT rather than 0; explicit non-default fill_value must be preserved; fully dense float NaN-fill cast to int must not raise IntCastingNaNError. Strategy is to build pandas at the buggy commit b65e5f2b8c5e and run the modified pandas/tests/arrays/sparse/test_astype.py tests, which should fail on buggy and pass on fixed.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython are listed as documented dependencies in readme:README.md with no version constraint; no era ceiling was stated, so no specific version is pinned here and the latest versions compatible with the buggy commit's build are used (unbounded, chosen by this strategy)
Cython is needed at build time for the editable build; pinned to whatever the build-system requirements in pyproject.toml at b65e5f2b8c5e specify, since that file was not in the evidence

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision b65e5f2b8c5e, the parametrized test_astype_dt64_to_sparse_int64_fill_value fails at tm.assert_sp_array_equal because the NaT fill is converted to 0 (fill 0 instead of iNaT) for the string and/or SparseDtype path, and the fully-dense NaN-fill test fails with IntCastingNaNError; on the fixed revision (PR #66175) all three tests pass, meaning the transition is fail-to-pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: values = np.array(['NaT','2016-01-02','2016-01-03'], dtype='M8[ns]'); SparseArray(values).astype('Sparse[int64]') should have fill iNaT = np.iinfo(np.int64).min

input_output_examples.input: dti = pd.date_range('2016-01-01', periods=3); ser = pd.Series(dti); ser[0] = pd.NaT; sparse = pd.core.arrays.SparseArray(ser.values); sparse.astype('Sparse[int64]')
input_output_examples.expected_output: NaT mapped to iNaT: values [-9223372036854775808, 1451692800000000000, 1451779200000000000] consistent with dense ser._values.astype('int64')

input_output_examples.buggy_output: not applicable (dense path is the reference)

input_output_examples.input: sparse.astype('int64') on the same NaT-filled SparseArray
input_output_examples.buggy_output: ValueError: Cannot convert NaT values to integer

risks: The defect is numerical/dtype-conversion only, so it should not depend on CPU architecture, but the fail-to-pass transition depends on the buggy commit being checked out exactly; confirm HEAD is b65e5f2b8c5e before running, since the PR date is unknown and the test file layout may differ.

Platform dependence is not evidenced: no sanitiser, threading or architecture requirement appears in the evidence, so none is assumed; if the NaT-to-int conversion behaves differently on 32-bit platforms, transition may not occur there.

The PR date and NumPy version were not stated, so NumPy 2.x vs 1.x behaviour for datetime-to-int casting and for IntCastingNaNError could differ; if the buggy test does not fail, pin NumPy to the version contemporaneous with the commit.
Editable build with --no-build-isolation needs Cython and a compiler present; a build failure would block the transition entirely and is not a reproduction of the bug.
Test selection with -k fill_value may also match unrelated tests; the explicit test node IDs in reproducing_test should be used if the selection is ambiguous.

The explicit-fill test (fill_value=5) is expected to pass on buggy code only if the bug overrides fill; per the context the pre-fix behaviour overrode it, so it may fail on buggy as well, which is consistent with fail-to-pass but not separately verified.

oracle.reference_source: test assertions via tm.assert_sp_array_equal against SparseArray with dtype SparseDtype('int64', fill_value=iNaT) and dense values.astype('int64')
oracle.why: Integer conversion of NaT to iNaT is an exact sentinel mapping, so exact equality is the oracle; no floating tolerance is involved.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy b65e5f2b8c5e, the string 'Sparse[int64]' path (and/or SparseDtype('int64') via Series.astype) yields fill 0 instead of iNaT, so tm.assert_sp_array_equal fails on the fill_value comparison; the fully dense NaN-fill case raises IntCastingNaNError during astype, failing the test with an exception.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision from PR #66175, the conversion maps NaT to iNaT only when the fill is NA, the target fill is not NA, and npoints != len(self); explicit fill 5 is preserved and the fully dense float NaN-fill case skips conversion, so all three tests pass.
